name: Aperiodic Pavement
desc: A quasicrystal pavement running away to a hazed horizon — rhombs of cut stone that never once repeat, every joint inlaid with a brass strip that flares as a low raking light travels up the hall.

energy.doc: light contrast + joint weight + walk rate

scale.doc: rhomb size vs frame (2.2 = a few colossal slabs underfoot)

density.doc: how far the pavement recedes before the haze takes it, and the stone tooth in each face

fold.doc: grid families -> symmetry: 5 = 10-fold Penrose rhombs, 6 = 12-fold dodecagonal, 7 = 14-fold, 4 = 8-fold octagonal

inlay.doc: brass inlay strip laid into every joint

phason.doc: slow perpendicular-space drift — distant rhombs quietly re-cut themselves

x.doc: vanishing point x as canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: brass-inlaid dark cut stone / pale polished terrazzo with aggregate / jewel-toned lapis / raw brutalist concrete / luminous additive rhombs on black (non-representational)

seed.doc: perpendicular-space phases — re-cuts the entire pavement
